subject: CCPA/CPRA role delineation, evidence request, and onshore fallback options
content:
From: Mira Patel <mira.patel@oxfordmed.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@oxfordmed.com
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify CCPA/CPRA classification and evidence for telemetry/log exports

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the earlier overview. Before we can greenlight the pilot, our legal/privacy team needs a clearer record that Redwood will qualify as a "service provider" (not an operator) under CCPA/CPRA for the types of requests we'll be sending. Specifically we need:

- A short explanation of Redwood's role for this engagement (processing-only, no independent profiling or primary use rights).
- Evidence that telemetry/log exports containing user identifiers are transient and will be treated in a way consistent with the SP obligations (retention bounds, deletion pathways).
- A current list of subprocessors and which ones are US-onshore vs offshore.
- Confirmation of whether Redwood will ever "sell" personal information as defined by CCPA; if not, a statement to that effect.

Can you send those items or an attestation that we can include as an exhibit to the addendum? Also want to know whether Redwood can offer an onshore fallback for telemetry exports if a specific subprocessor is offshore.

If it helps, our HubSpot deal is HB-4921 and legal would prefer a one-page attestation plus a CSV of subprocessors.

Best,
Mira

---

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Mira Patel <mira.patel@oxfordmed.com>
Cc: legal@oxfordmed.com
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify CCPA/CPRA classification and evidence for telemetry/log exports

Hi Mira,

Thanks — happy to outline and provide the artifacts you mentioned. High level answers first:

- Role: Redwood will act as a service provider (CCPA/CPRA) / processor (DPA) for the Oxford Medical Systems integration. We process requests on your instruction and do not use customer data to independently build a business about customers.
- Sales: Redwood does not "sell" personal information as defined by CCPA. We will include explicit language in the addendum.
- Telemetry & logs: We implement transient KV/prefix caching and aggregated telemetry. Identifiable request logs are retained only as required for debugging/security and are subject to a 30-day retention window by default (configurable, can be shortened for enterprise agreements). Deletion pathways are documented and we can provide a removal confirmation for specific request ids.
- Subprocessors: attaching a CSV with current subprocessors and their region. We can flag onshore-only options where available.

Attachments included: redwood_ddr_summary.pdf (short DDR + retention/telemetry note), subprocessor_inventory.csv (name, role, region), attestation_template.docx (one-page attestation we can sign).

Next steps I propose:
- We'll draft a one-page attestation referencing CCPA/CPRA service provider commitments and an exhibit showing retention periods.
- Legal: if you want to redline our standard US privacy addendum, please send it and I'll loop in our legal ops.
- If an onshore fallback is required for specific subprocessors, we can scope that as a configuration and provide a project timeline (typically 4-6 weeks to stand up onshore routing for telemetry in our Dedicated pool).

I'll also paste a short, plain-language attestation below (draft) so you can share internally: 

"Redwood Inference acts only as a service provider (as defined under the CCPA/CPRA) with respect to data transmitted by Oxford Medical Systems to the Redwood platform. Redwood will not sell personal information, will process data only at Oxford's direction, and will delete or return personal information in accordance with agreed retention schedules. Redwood maintains documented subprocessors and will provide reasonable notice of changes."

I'll follow up with a formal attestation and the CSV. Let me know if your team needs SOC 2 evidence as well — we can provide our SOC 2 report via secure link.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
(h) 415-555-0142

Attachments: redwood_ddr_summary.pdf (PDF, 2 pages) | subprocessor_inventory.csv (CSV, 1 file) | attestation_template.docx (DOCX, 1 file)

---

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 4 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Clarify CCPA/CPRA classification and evidence for telemetry/log exports — coordination

Aditya, Laura — forwarding Mira's request. OxfordMed (HB-4921) has asked for a signed attestation, subprocessor CSV, and an option for an onshore fallback for telemetry. Legal will likely want a signed one-page attestation plus a redline to their US addendum.

Suggested owner split:
- Aditya: prepare the one-page attestation and attach our standard attestation_template.docx. Confirm signature authority and whether we route to legal ops for signature. (Due: Tue 2026-09-07)
- Laura: prepare a redline of the US privacy addendum based on our standard proposed language (preserve service provider/processor language, add explicit non-sale clause and telemetry retention exhibit). Add a clause for onshore fallback SOW and estimated lead time 4-6 weeks with optional fees. (Due: Wed 2026-09-08)
- Hannah: I'll deliver subprocessor_inventory.csv and the DDR summary now; if they request SOC 2 I will share the secure link.

Also: propose we add a short SLA footnote for deletion confirmations (48 hrs to provide deletion proof for PII-containing request ids). Think that's reasonable for the pilot.

Action items:
- Aditya: draft + signable attestation (attestation_template.docx).
- Laura: redline addendum; include explicit non-sale language and retention exhibit.
- Hannah: confirm onshore fallback feasibility and provide an approximate cost/time estimate for OxfordMed.

Thanks — Hannah

--- Forwarded message from Mira Patel ---
From: Mira Patel <mira.patel@oxfordmed.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify CCPA/CPRA classification and evidence for telemetry/log exports

Hannah,

Thanks for the quick responses and the artifacts — our legal team reviewed the draft attestation and the subprocessor CSV. A couple of follow-ups: 

- We can accept the one-page attestation but need the retention window expressed as "identifiable request logs retained no longer than 30 days by default; configurable to 7 days for covered customers." Please update the attestation to include those numbers.
- Please add an explicit sentence: "Redwood will not sell personal information as defined under California Civil Code §1798.140(o)."
- For subprocessors: can you flag which entries in the CSV are "onshore available" (i.e., we can route them to a US-only instance) vs not?
- Onshore fallback: we are OK with a 4–6 week timeline if you can commit in writing with a scope/fee range. Please include a short SOW paragraph we can attach to the addendum.

If you can send revised attestation (signed) and a redline that includes the non-sale text, retention exhibit, and the SOW paragraph, we should be able to proceed to legal sign-off quickly.

Appreciate it — Mira

[End of thread]
